Furthermore, an item bank based on Revised Bloom's Taxonomy was created. Additionally, the validity of the instruments used was evaluated using the Rasch model. We conducted an analysis of User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) data to evaluate the overall user experience of both the conventional and CAT tests, and the statistics indicate that the web-based CAT offers a more user-friendly experience. The study also utilized the concordance rate to gauge the similarity of data responses among the conventional, CAT, and self-assessment tests concerning VAK learning styles. The findings indicate that the proposed method exhibits an 87% similarity with self-assessment and shows significant potential.

articleTitle: Social Media Analytics Overview on University Marketing of Private University and Public University in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: Indonesia's educational landscape is witnessing remarkable growth with an abundance of universities, both public and private, vying for the attention of high school graduates. This study delves into the challenges students encounter when making informed academic decisions and the fierce competition faced by universities in attracting and retaining students. In a digital age, universities emphasize the importance of strong brand images, utilizing social media to convey their values. This study focuses on Instagram as a platform for exploring university marketing strategies, utilizing secondary data obtained from the official university account in Indonesia through descriptive research methods. Data collection involved the utilization of phlanx.com, inflact.com, and analisa.io websites. The discussion delves into our perspective as researchers on how to articulate the distilled information verbally. A crucial finding shows that University J is outstanding in its promotion on Instagram, causing an increase in interaction and maintaining contact between students. University J recorded a remarkable engagement rate of 1.88%, outshining its rivals by attaining student appreciation and visual appeal's captivating content.

articleTitle: A Study of Battery Monitoring System Based LoRaWAN for Public Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: Public Electric vehicles have been used in many cities around the world. Lithium batteries are mostly used as an energy source for those electric vehicles due to their efficiency and versatility. For safety reason, Battery Management System (BMS) is required for comprehensive monitoring and fault diagnosis of a lithium battery pack. To monitor the BMS operation, a remote BMS monitoring system is a solution. Low-power long-Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN) has been deployed in many applications that require low-power, long-range communication due to its unique transmission modulation. Applying a LoRaWAN technology to fleet of electric buses can be cost-effective solution for many large cities around the world. Moreover, there is no additional cost for utilizing the LoRaWAN frequency spectrum in many countries around the world since LoRaWAN usually operated on unlicensed spectrum. In this work, a BMS monitoring system based on (LoRaWAN) protocol is developed. Electrical parameters from a BMS including individual cell voltage, current, temperatures, State of Charge (SoC) and state of Health (SoH) are transmitted over the LoRaWAN at AS923-925 frequency plan (923-925 MHz). The communication range analysis was performed based on Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) and a monitoring system dashboard.

articleTitle: Development of Automatic Solar-Powered Microcontroller- Based Algae Collector Using Pixy2 Cam in Taal Lake
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: Taal Lake in Batangas Philippines has a vital role in providing aquatic resources, sustaining the livelihoods of fisherman, and functioning as a renowned tourist attraction. Nevertheless, the exponential proliferation of algae leads to issues such as the obstruction of sunlight, which hinders the growth of aquatic plants, the blockage of fish gills resulting in suffocation, and the obstruction of the scenic view of the lake. This study focuses on the persistent problem of harmful algal blooms (HABs) in Taal Lake, Batangas. It suggests the use of an automated system to gather algae as a way to reduce the spread of decomposing algae. Harmful algal blooms (HABs) provide ecological risks and also jeopardize human health by causing the accumulation of toxins in the food chain. A solar-powered boat was developed with Arduino technology, incorporating algorithms, sensors, a microcontroller, and a GSM module to detect, collect, and control algae. The Pixy2 Cam can accurately identify green algae present on the water's surface, providing guidance for the system's movement. Additionally, an ultrasonic sensor is used to detect the buildup of algae in the tank. Smart tag technology enabled location tracking, while SMS messages would inform users when the tank reached its full capacity. Based on conducted experiments, the prototype demonstrated effectiveness in detecting colors, collecting algae, sending SMS messages, and tracking location. User feedback has confirmed that the device performs well, which supports its potential use as an effective method for addressing Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) in Taal Lake. In conclusion, this innovative automaton system has the potential to tackle environmental problems associated with algae blooms and encourage sustainable approaches to lake management.

articleTitle: Analytical Challenges of Quantum and Classical Computing in Thailand: A Comparative Exploration of Machine Learning Through Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: This research explores the integration of classical and quantum machine learning (QML) for classification tasks, focusing on applications in Thailand. We evaluate QML algorithms, including Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC), Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC), and Quantum Neural Network (QNN), against the classical Support Vector Machine (SVM) using the Iris and Wine datasets on IBM's Qiskit platform. Our analysis highlights the trade-offs between accuracy and preprocessing time for quantum encoding, noting that while some QML algorithms achieve high accuracy, their preprocessing times are significantly longer than those of classical SVM. This underscores current limitations in QML for practical classification tasks. However, the study also identifies future opportunities for QML applications in sectors like healthcare, materials science, logistics, and financial modeling in Thailand. This research contributes to the field by providing a comparative analysis of QML and classical algorithms, revealing that QML, despite its high accuracy, is often hindered by lengthy preprocessing. It also emphasizes QML's potential to address specific technological challenges in Thailand.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Location-Routing Network Optimization for Pre-Disaster Planning: A Case Study in the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: A significant issue influencing the humanitarian supply chain (HSC) is facility location. The logistics of moving relief supplies from the main distribution center (DC) to distribution hubs (DHs) to evacuation centers (ECs), which need to be strategically placed and easily accessible from the affected areas, serve as the inspiration for this paper's location model. This enables the HSC to be prepared for any calamity and respond to it as quickly as possible. This work presents a multi-objective location-routing network optimization model designed for the pre-disaster phase. It focuses on optimizing locations of distribution hubs and evacuation centers to manage mandatory evacuations within the allowable response time. The model aims to minimize infrastructure costs while maximizing the coverage of evacuation centers to nearby residential areas, ensuring that relocations are carried out promptly during emergencies. A case study showcasing the model's effectiveness was conducted using AnyLogistix (ALX) software. Our findings identify the optimal placement of evacuation centers and distribution hubs, achieving cost reduction and improved response times.

articleTitle: Exploring Human Factors in Global Supply Chains to Mitigate Crises in Swiss Industrial SMEs: A Power Electronics Company Research Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: This study examines vulnerabilities in the global supply chain and aims to minimize their impact on Swiss industrial SMEs, with a particular focus on a given Power Electronics Company (PEC). An in-depth analysis of a case study, based on semi-directed interviews, is used to explore the weaknesses that disrupted the supply chain, with a particular emphasis on the human (tacit) factor. Our research examines the challenges faced by industrial SMEs in pre-crisis orchestration, responses during COVID-19, and post-crisis adaptations. We consider the unique human elements intertwined with technological advances. Drawing on insights from risk assessment, customer experience, and knowledge management literature, this article proposes strategic measures for Swiss SMEs to strengthen the resilience of their supply chain. The focus is on the human factor rather than purely digitized and/or AI-based innovations. The article provides valuable insights and actionable strategies for industrial SMEs facing the uncertainties of the globalized business landscape.

articleTitle: Contextual Based E-Tourism Application: A Personalized Attraction Recommendation System for Destination Branding and Cultivating Tourism Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative automated application designed to offer users personalized attraction recommendations tailored to their interests and current situations. Utilizing a contextual model and advanced machine learning techniques, the system constructs a comprehensive user profile by considering factors like historical behavior, current context, and demographic data. This approach addresses limitations observed in conventional personalized recommendation systems, including challenges in suggesting attractions for new users, providing comparable recommendations, and incorporating appropriate weighting. By integrating multi-dimensional user models based on context, the system enhances the platform's personalization and adaptability, ultimately contributing to the augmentation of Destination Branding and the cultivation of enriched Tourism. The research yields practical solutions for optimizing tourism services' personalization and introduces improvements in e-tourism recommender systems, carrying significant implications for both industry practitioners and academic researchers.

articleTitle: Technology Acceptance: A Case Study of Digital Herbal Platform and Health Data Innovation In Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: In this research, the factors affecting the adoption of digital technology in digital herbal platforms and data innovations for healthcare in Thailand were thoroughly explored. It focuses on people who are interested in herbal remedies and alternative health care, as well as young people who are not yet familiar with the use of herbs. The main objective is to develop the platform as a comprehensive center for the distribution of herbal medicines. Support community engagement and promote online medical tourism. The results of data analysis from a group of users interested in herbs and alternative health care helped us apply inbound marketing technology to develop a “Digital Herbal Hub” that emphasizes convenience and covers all genders, all ages. This includes promoting online medical tourism in Thailand

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Use of the Cancer Care Collaboration (CCC) Application, Which Provides Personalized Content and Treatment for Cancer Patients Based on Symptoms in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to: 1) study the behavior of accepting the use of CCC application in Thailand 2) study the factors influencing acceptance and usage of CCC technology in Thailand 3) study the outcomes of accessing cancer treatment and knowledge gained from the CCC application in Thailand. This research uses the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) The process for quantitative data analysis collected through an online questionnaire from a sample group of 401 individuals in Thailand, including cancer patients, their family or relatives, and those with cancer awareness. The research findings reveal that questionnaire respondents have the intention to use the CCC application, with the performance expectancy factor showing the highest correlation with the intention to use the application. Respondents anticipate that using the CCC application will support access to cancer treatment and enhance their knowledge, aligning with the application's objectives. Subsidiary factors include the convenience of using the application, social influence, and expectations regarding usage.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Nykaa User's Satisfaction: A Case Study of Online Beauty Shopping Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 5th Technology Innovation Management and Engineering Science International Conference (TIMES-iCON)
abstract: In an era where e-commerce has become integral to the retail landscape, the user-friendliness and overall design of digital platforms play a pivotal role in shaping user satisfaction. Nykaa, a prominent player in the beauty and cosmetic industry, has established a significant online presence. Nykaa is an Indian beauty retailer that sells cosmetics and wellness goods online and in physical stores. Nykaa, founded in 2012 by former investment banker Falguni Nayar, has grown to become one of India's biggest beauty destinations, offering a diverse selection of products such as makeup, skincare, hair care, fragrances, and wellness items. The research objective of this paper is to identify factors influencing Nykaa users' satisfaction. The goal is to identify particular areas to improve overall user satisfaction. A convenience sampling strategy was employed, collecting data from a sample of 385 individuals via Google Forms. Descriptive statistics were utilized in the research design, and data analysis was conducted using the SPSS program. The findings indicate users' satisfaction with Nykaa's services is neutral regarding various dimensions such as product offerings, website navigation and over user satisfaction. To analyze hypothesized relationships, inferential statistics, specifically regression analysis, were employed. The results of the research revealed that functionality and features, as well as navigation and information architecture, significantly influence user satisfaction. The conclusions drawn offer insightful information to inform Nykaa's digital strategy for enhancing their online platforms and ultimately improving Nykaa users’ satisfaction.
